<thought>From the spectrum, the most distinctive isotopic feature is a combined M+2 intensity of about 5–6 % of the base peak (peaks at m/z ≈ 237 and ≈ 238). This magnitude matches the characteristic 34S isotope (≈4 % of the monoisotopic intensity) and is far lower than the ≈33 % expected for a single chlorine atom or the ≈100 % for bromine. No clear 1:1 M+2 pattern (bromine) or 3:1 M+2 pattern (chlorine) is observed. Therefore, sulfur is the only element whose isotopic distribution can be definitively identified from the data.</thought>
<final_answer>['S']</final_answer>
